purpose: Authoritative implementation queue for ROOT Kata curriculum agents. Agents execute this plan; they do not redesign the syllabus during routine runs.
selection_rule: Within current_milestone, implement the first planned unit in listed order whose prerequisites are already implemented. Never skip a blocked earlier unit or invent a replacement without reviewer feedback.

milestones.title: C++ entry and first ROOT object
milestones.learning_outcome: A newcomer can run real C++, inspect simple values, apply a cut, and fill a first TH1D.

milestones.title: Histogram literacy, graphs, functions and fitting
milestones.learning_outcome: The learner stops treating a histogram as a picture and can reason about binning, bin contents, overflow, simple ROOT functions, graphs and fit results.

units.competency: Inspect entries, bin contents and summary statistics of a TH1D instead of judging it only by its drawing.
units.acceptance: Visible tests distinguish entries from selected bin contents and verify at least one bin-level observation.

units.competency: Choose or diagnose a histogram range by reasoning about underflow and overflow.
units.acceptance: A wrong range produces observable under/overflow behavior and the correct solution preserves the intended sample representation.

units.competency: Distinguish adding observations with Fill from manually changing bin contents with SetBinContent.
units.acceptance: Tests expose the semantic difference through entries and bin contents rather than API-name trivia.

units.competency: Represent paired measurements with TGraph and inspect point coordinates.
units.acceptance: The graph contains the intended ordered pairs and tests validate points, not cosmetic drawing settings.

units.competency: Represent a mathematical model with TF1 and reason about its parameters and evaluation.
units.acceptance: Tests verify model behavior at selected x values and parameter changes.

units.competency: Fit a simple peaked distribution and interpret fitted location and width as model results.
units.acceptance: A deterministic sample yields fit parameters in justified tolerances and feedback points to model/data mismatch rather than syntax.

units.competency: Recognize when a composite peak-plus-background model is needed and configure a multi-parameter fit.
units.acceptance: The learner constructs the intended composite model and obtains a fit that recovers the salient peak behavior within deterministic tolerances.

milestones.title: ROOT files and the event-dataset mental model
milestones.learning_outcome: The learner can persist and retrieve ROOT objects and understands a TTree as a columnar event dataset rather than a mysterious file object.

units.competency: Write a named ROOT object to a TFile and close the file cleanly.
units.acceptance: A produced ROOT file can be reopened and contains the expected object with preserved contents.

units.competency: Retrieve a ROOT object by name and verify what was actually stored.
units.acceptance: Tests include a correct key and a diagnostic case where the requested object name is wrong or absent.

units.competency: Inspect a TTree's entry count and available branches to connect event rows with dataset columns.

source.concept: TTree, TBranch and columnar event data

units.acceptance: The learner identifies entries and branches from a small bundled deterministic ROOT file without writing a manual branch loop.

milestones.title: RDataFrame analysis essentials
milestones.learning_outcome: The learner can express a small analysis as query, Define, Filter and actions, and understands lazy execution well enough to avoid accidental repeated event loops.

units.competency: Construct an RDataFrame from a tree and inspect available columns before writing analysis expressions.
units.acceptance: Tests verify the expected dataset and columns are discovered from the supplied file.

units.competency: Create a derived column from existing quantities with Define.
units.acceptance: The derived column has expected values on a deterministic sample and is used by a downstream action.

units.competency: Apply a physically meaningful numerical selection with Filter and reason about which rows survive.
units.acceptance: Boundary cases make an incorrect >= versus > choice visibly fail.

units.competency: Use Count and Mean as actions on the transformed dataset and distinguish transformations from results.
units.acceptance: Tests verify both surviving row count and an aggregate derived from the same filtered node.

units.competency: Book a Histo1D from a dataframe column with intentional binning.
units.acceptance: The result histogram reflects the selected dataset and expected binning, entries and integral semantics.

units.competency: Book multiple actions before dereferencing results so one event loop can produce them together.
units.acceptance: A deliberately eager implementation causes more runs than the target implementation; tests expose the run-count consequence.

units.competency: Recognize and compose the required Define, Filter and actions for a small unfamiliar analysis question.
units.acceptance: The exercise asks for an analysis outcome rather than naming every API call; visible tests verify derived quantities, selection and result together.

milestones.title: Collections and object-level selections
milestones.learning_outcome: The learner can reason about per-event collections, vectorized quantities and masks, then turn selected objects into analysis distributions.

units.competency: Use RVec element-wise arithmetic and understand that vector operations preserve object correspondence.
units.acceptance: Tests compare derived vector values for multiple events including an empty collection.

units.competency: Build a boolean RVec mask and select only objects satisfying a condition.
units.acceptance: Boundary and empty-collection cases verify that selected objects correspond exactly to the mask.

units.competency: Derive transverse momentum from px and py and apply an independent object-quality mask before histogramming.
units.acceptance: Tests ensure the learner does not confuse the quantity being computed with the quantity used for object selection.

units.competency: Turn selected object collections into an RDataFrame histogram and interpret the resulting distribution.
units.acceptance: An end-to-end deterministic sample verifies object mask, derived quantity and histogram contents together.

milestones.title: Reusable analysis workflows and performance habits
milestones.learning_outcome: The learner can persist processed datasets, inspect cutflow, reuse C++ helpers and make informed choices about ROOT's execution model.

units.competency: Persist only the intended processed columns with Snapshot and reopen the result.
units.acceptance: The output file contains the expected tree, row count and selected columns, without unintended columns.

units.competency: Name sequential filters and use Report to reason about selection efficiency through a cutflow.
units.acceptance: Visible tests verify per-cut all/pass counts and expose a badly ordered or incorrect cut.

units.competency: Move a nontrivial reusable calculation into a small C++ helper and call it from Define.
units.acceptance: The helper is pure, tested independently, and its derived column matches expected values.

units.competency: Recognize why user code executed by implicit multithreading must avoid unsafe shared mutable state.
units.acceptance: The exercise rewards a deterministic pure implementation; it must not depend on flaky timing or race reproduction.

units.competency: Use Redefine intentionally when the semantic meaning of an existing column is preserved but its values must change.
units.acceptance: Tests verify the downstream analysis sees the redefined values under the original column name.

units.competency: Run independent RDataFrame result graphs together when an analysis has multiple samples.

source.concept: multiple concurrent RDataFrame runs with RunGraphs

units.acceptance: Two deterministic sample graphs produce their expected independent results without serial result dereferencing before RunGraphs.

milestones.title: Independent ROOT analysis transfer
milestones.learning_outcome: The learner can recognize which familiar ROOT operations solve a compact analysis problem without being told the API sequence.

units.competency: Inspect an unfamiliar small ROOT dataset, derive one useful quantity, apply a selection and produce an interpretable histogram plus cutflow.
units.acceptance: The prompt states the scientific/data goal but does not prescribe the exact ROOT operation sequence; tests validate the final selection and outputs.

units.competency: Diagnose a plausible analysis whose result is wrong because of a cut boundary, histogram range or eager RDataFrame execution choice.
units.acceptance: The learner must identify the causal defect from observable output rather than merely fill in missing syntax.

milestones.title: Optional ecosystem extensions
milestones.learning_outcome: Not part of the autonomous core queue until a product need justifies them.

units.competency: Python Unified Histogram Interface interoperability.
units.acceptance: Deferred because ROOT Kata's current core is C++/ROOT and this source section is Python-specific.

units.competency: Create/export RDataFrame datasets through NumPy interoperability.
units.acceptance: Deferred until Python interoperability is a learner goal for ROOT Kata.

units.competency: Execute RDataFrame through Dask/Spark backends.
units.acceptance: Deferred because distributed infrastructure is outside the current portable 80/20 learner path.
